questions.question: A product photo should keep its original pixels except for a distracting sign inside a mask. Which task is this?
options: Inpainting within the masked region
Unconditional text-to-image generation
Image classification over the whole photo
Outpainting beyond the original canvas
questions.explanation: Inpainting regenerates pixels inside the selected mask while keeping the rest of the source image, matching a localized sign removal. Outpainting instead extends beyond the original canvas, so it would change the wrong region for this task.

questions.question: What extra inputs does a proper 9-channel inpainting U-Net receive alongside the noisy latent?
options: Encoded source image and a one-channel mask
Text tokens and speaker embeddings
Two copies of the noisy latent only
A discriminator score and timestep label
questions.explanation: A proper inpainting U-Net concatenates the noisy four-channel latent with a four-channel encoded source and a one-channel mask, giving 9 channels total. The source and mask reveal what is around the hole and where generation is needed.

questions.question: How does SDEdit’s starting noise level affect fidelity to the source image?
options: Lower t/T preserves more of the source
The starting t/T changes only image resolution
Higher t/T preserves more of the source
The starting t/T has no effect on source identity
questions.explanation: SDEdit adds noise up to the chosen t and then denoises; lower t injects less corruption, preserving more source structure. Higher t starts closer to noise, leaving more room for a new prompt to change the image.

questions.question: What is RePaint’s training requirement in the lesson?
options: It requires a U-Net retrained on nine-channel masked inputs
It replaces the denoiser with a cycle-consistency GAN
It uses a standard diffusion model and resamples during reverse steps
It needs paired source and target images for each edit
questions.explanation: RePaint uses a standard unconditional diffusion denoiser and periodically jumps back to a noisier state to resample during reverse generation. The specially trained nine-channel U-Net is the proper inpainting model, not a RePaint requirement.

questions.question: A small masked edit looks oversaturated under classifier-free guidance. What should be adjusted?
options: Lower CFG for the small mask
Increase the mask until it covers the full image
Raise CFG to the maximum setting
Replace the source image with pure noise
questions.explanation: High CFG on a small masked region can overemphasize the prompt and saturate that patch. Lowering guidance addresses this; increasing CFG would amplify the same oversaturation.

questions.question: To extend an image canvas while keeping the original content, how should the mask be used?
options: Mask both regions and ask the VAE to reconstruct them
Mask the new canvas area and keep the original unmasked
Mask the original content and freeze the new canvas
Remove the mask and regenerate the full image
questions.explanation: Outpainting flips which area is masked: regenerate the new canvas while leaving original content unmasked as context. Masking the original would invite changes to the image the task says to keep.
